# humlook_masks.txt: which texels of the armed humanoids' skins the recolours dye (humlook.txt; vr_humlook.cpp).
# Made from each skin's 8-bit palette rows as the model loads: no texture is changed or copied. The Texture Studio
# (Debug > Tools) writes it.
#   rows <key> <class> <row>...      a key's palette rows (0..15: index / 16) of that class; the others: none
#        key: grunt, enforcer, knight, dknight (their bodies), pack (a worn backpack); class: clothes, pack, none
#   skinrows <model> <skin> <key> <class> <row>...   one skin's own rows instead of its key's
#   paint <model> <skin> <key> <w> <h> <class> <texels>...   texels painted by hand (y * w + x, ranges a-b): clothes,
#        pack, or never (left as it is whatever its row); only on a skin of that size
#   flesh <row>...                  the flesh's rows: never dyed (default 7)
#   fleshnear <share> <radius>      a dyed row's texel left as it is where this share of the texels within the radius
#        are flesh (an arm's or a face's highlights on the uniforms' tans; 0: off)
# Their palette rows (scratch analysis, ROUND25 "humrepl2"): the uniforms and leather are rows 1 and 10 (browns, tans),
# flesh row 7 (peach), blood row 4 (reds): rows keep faces and flesh out where a hue band could not.
flesh 7
fleshnear 0.35 2
rows grunt    clothes 1 10
rows enforcer clothes 1 3 10
rows knight   clothes 1 10
rows dknight  clothes 1
rows pack     pack    1
